title: Where he worked when World War II started
summary: Worked in the Quarter, with George Williams on Napoleon Avenue, Popeye's and Club Arlington with Billy and De De.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years

blocks.x: Well, where were you working when, uh, World War II started? Do you remember? World War II when it started?
I think I was in the quarters. I think I was in the quarters. I think I was in the quarters of World War II. Uh, it wasn't that the last round, though.
You were there a long time?

Yeah, that's right. I used to work, uh, you had another place. We worked in Napoleon Avenue in Chapa Tour. Uh, probably by the name of George Heffler had that club out there. And he'd work there regularly. I was with George Williams up there. I worked there. World War II, I'm trying to think. I think I was at the, uh, World War II, uh, I think it was either last round up or at Popeye's on Decatur Street. I worked out there for quite a long time with, uh, Kid Howard out there. Because Bill and D.D. was working at the corner from where we were at. Then I worked with them at the nightclub on Ramp. What's that? Club Arlington.

Arlington. Right where, uh, Woolworth's now on Ramp on Canal. Uh-huh. Right in the middle of the block they had a club they called, uh, Club Arlington. And I worked there. Oh, Arlington. Arlington. I worked there six months with them. Bill and D.D. and Alba Jow.
